title: Separate residual-path effects from parameter-count effects in a shallow MLP
description: Compare an MLP with a residual path against a parameter-matched MLP without that path. Treat the claim as a human hypothesis that still needs literature grounding.
gap: Whether the residual path itself explains an observed gain under matched training resources

hypothesis.claim: A residual path improves optimization beyond the effect of adding the same number of parameters
hypothesis.predicted_effect: Lower validation error under matched training resources

experiment_plan: Implement a residual variant and a matched control in the editable train module; keep the frozen scorer, data split, seeds and training resources fixed.
novelty_rationale: Unverified human proposal; retrieve and inspect related work before making a novelty claim.

design.mechanism: The residual path changes optimization dynamics rather than merely increasing capacity
design.intervention: Add or remove the residual path while controlling parameter count
assumptions: Parameter-matched controls can be constructed in the available engine
design.minimal_test: Validation-only comparison of the intervention and its matched control
design.kill_criterion: The apparent benefit disappears after matching training resources and capacity
design.resource_risk: The architecture must first be implemented and checked; a crash is not evidence against the hypothesis
novelty_queries: shallow MLP residual connections parameter matched optimization
